13.0.0.en: "By the sea side": it is the Sea of Galilee.

13.0.1.en: The crowds followed Christ as was their custom, to enjoy His life-giving teachings, and as their number increased, and He was near the shore of the sea, He entered one of the boats and moved a little away from the land in it, so that it became a pulpit for Him from which to speak, while the crowds sat on the shore to listen to Him.

13.0.2.en: How great is the simplicity of Christ and His humility! He teaches on the mountain, or on the shore, or stands in a boat which He regards as a pulpit for His teachings. For the most important thing to Him is to win the love of the crowds, and convey His spiritual teachings to them.

13.0.3.en: He went out of the house in which He was staying, which signifies the Church, from which He went out into the world to visit His people, and He entered the sea, which signifies the world, but He stood in a boat, which signifies the human soul in which He dwells, and shows Himself from it to others, as He does through His believing children who are the light of the world.

13.1.0.en: "Spake many things unto them": it is understood that He gave many examples, some of which are recorded in the Holy Bible. "Parables": an illustration of the spiritual truth by a practical, real story, to bring the meaning near to the mind of the hearer. "The sower": he is God.

13.1.1.en: The sower used the seeds, which are His word that He gives to the different soils, which represent the kinds of people, each differing from the other in his receiving of His word.

13.1.2.en: The sower went forth to sow, for God's work is goodness; He casts His word to all in the hope that it may bear fruit. Likewise the children of God, their work is doing good to all, regardless of how much others respond to this good.

13.2.0.en: The first kind of soil is the farm path that passes beside the fields, which is raised above them and hard and not prepared for planting, and is always trodden by the feet of passersby.

13.2.1.en: It points to the proud human soul that has not been prepared by plowing to receive the word of God, that is, self-examination and repentance.

13.2.2.en: And it is hard, so it points to hardness of heart and rejection of the word of God, and it is trodden by all, that is, all the lusts of the world enter it, for it has no walls to protect it, that is, it is not fortified by the Church; so when the word of God was cast into it, it rejoiced in it quickly but the heart did not receive it, and soon the birds of the air swooped down on it and ate the seeds. The birds point to the demons that steal the word, because the heart is affected temporarily, and quickly loses this effect, because of its pride and its not repenting of its various lusts.

13.3.0.en: The second kind of soil is the stony ground, but it has a thin surface layer of earth, so its appearance is as though it were good farmland, and its reality is that it is stones that refuse any planting in it.

13.3.1.en: It points to hardness of heart like stone, and to the worship of idols of stone, that is, the worship of the money and positions of this world, which are like idols to which a person clings, for although he has a surface soil in which the seeds grow a little, when the roots try to extend, they cannot because of the stones, and when the sun rises these little plants dry up and die.

13.3.2.en: It also signifies hypocritical souls, which have the appearance of good soil and the reality of stone.

13.3.3.en: And it signifies hearts attached to the world, which receive the word for a short time, and when trials come upon them, like the rays of the sun, they dry up quickly and the word of God dies in them, for they are hard, selfish hearts that do not love God from within.

13.4.0.en: The third kind of soil is good soil suitable for planting, but full of thorns, that is, the heart's concerns for the world and its lusts.

13.4.1.en: So when the word of God is cast into it, it grows, but the growth of the thorns and foreign weeds is stronger than it, so they crowd its roots in the ground and it finds no nourishment, and the thorns and weeds cover it from above, so the rays of the sun do not reach it, and they choke it and it dies.

13.4.2.en: It points to the danger of keeping the lusts of sin in the heart, because they hinder the work of the word of God, so that a person does not benefit from it. And the remedy of course is repentance and removing the thorns of sin, and then the word can have an effect on these souls.

13.5.0.en: The fourth kind of soil is the good ground suitable for planting, and if the word of God is cast into it, it grows and bears fruit. And the amount of fruit differs according to the fertility of the ground and its response to the word, for all are children of the Kingdom, but one star differs from another in how it benefits from and applies the word of God.

13.6.0.en: Christ affirmed the importance of hearing His word with the two ears, that is, the outer ear, and the inner ear which is the heart, in order to understand and apply the word.

13.6.1.en: God offers His love and grace to all people, but what matters is that you respond to it, so do not reject the word of God that He sends you, whether in the Holy Bible or the teachings of the Church and the guidance of your father of confession, or on the tongues of those around you.

13.6.2.en: Receive the word for yourself and not for teaching others, and try to apply it in your life, and trust that every striving to carry out the word of God is very precious to Him, and He supports you to complete it, and rewards you for it.

13.7.0.en: "Came": after the crowds departed, a few remained and came forward to Christ to ask Him.

13.7.1.en: "The disciples": they are the Twelve and another small group of those attached to Christ, as appears from (Mk 4:10), and they are like the seventy Apostles and the Marys.

13.7.2.en: "It is given unto you": a special grace given to those who care to know God.

13.7.3.en: "The mysteries of the kingdom of heaven": that is, how God reigns over the heart, for the knowledge of God is above the human mind, but God by His grace gives understanding to those ready to receive Him.

13.7.4.en: "Them": those who do not care about the word of God, because of their preoccupation with material things, so their knowledge is always superficial. Christ spoke to the crowds in parables close to their lives, that they might understand the idea and be affected by it, because in the hardness of their hearts they will reject direct speech, but the parables from their own lives they may accept, and so submit to the word of God. But the disciples, because of their readiness to obey Christ, He explained the parables to them in direct spiritual language, for whoever has spiritual readiness is given more and more knowledge of God. But whoever has no readiness and keeps rejecting, even the parable he does not understand and will reject it, and the little spiritual understanding he has he will lose through his pride and his attachment to the material world.

13.8.0.en: "Seeing they see not, and hearing they hear not": despite their seeing Christ and hearing His teachings, they do not grasp the depths of the words in order to apply them in their lives, but are content with superficial knowledge. And more than this, they may even reject the words and their spiritual meanings, because of their attachment to their material lusts and their pride. "This people's heart is waxed gross": that is, it became bound to earthly lusts, and was no longer tender and open to being affected by the word of God.

13.8.1.en: "Dull of hearing": that is, they became unable to understand the word of God, because lusts have deafened their ears, and they want to hear only what pleases them.

13.8.2.en: "That I should heal them": that is, I accept their repentance, and set their lives right so that they become spiritual.

13.8.3.en: Although these crowds have outward eyes, and ears that distinguish letters, their hearts reject God; they awaited the awaited Messiah according to the prophecies, and when Christ became incarnate and came to them, they rejected Him because of the hardness of their hearts and their pride, and their attachment to earthly kingship and honor, so they lost spiritual understanding, as their great prophet Isaiah prophesied about them (Isa 6:10).

13.9.0.en: Christ praises His disciples for their understanding of His word, and their enjoying the sight of Him, and their faith that He is the awaited Messiah, and He even declares to them that the honor they received of seeing Him was desired by many prophets and godly men in the Old Testament who did not see Him, but received only the honor of prophesying about Him, and awaited the promise of its fulfillment while their souls were bound in Hades, until He came and accomplished redemption for them and saved them.

13.9.1.en: This is what you behold today, my brother, in the Church, and even receive true Body and Blood, and enjoy hearing the word of God in the Holy Bible, which all the men of God in the Old Testament longed to behold, so enjoy it, that you may live by it and in it, and be careful to attend the Liturgies from their beginning, and to receive the blessing of confession and Holy Communion always.

13.10.s.en: (3) The interpretation of the parable of the sower

13.10.0.en: "The word of the kingdom": the word of God which, if you understand it and apply it, makes your heart prepared for the reign of God over it.

13.10.1.en: "Understandeth it not": he refuses to understand the word of God, because of his preoccupation with material things.

13.10.3.en: "Catcheth away": that is, his being affected is very temporary, like an emotional reaction that passes quickly, and he applies nothing of what he heard in his life.

13.11.0.en: "Anon receiveth it": the quick being affected by the word of God, and the intention to apply it and begin to do so.

13.12.0.en: "Hath not root in himself": he has not striven in the way of God to carry out His word for a long time, that is, his being affected is emotional and superficial, and the heart is weak as a result of his life preoccupied with the world.

13.12.1.en: "Tribulation or persecution": that is, problems that try to prevent him from continuing to carry out the commandment. "Is offended": that is, he leaves the commandments of God and returns to his life bound to the world.

13.13.0.en: "The care of this world": anxiety and preoccupation with acquiring material things and various lusts. "The deceitfulness of riches": pride resulting from the material things a person possesses, so he feels he is better than others. "Choke the word": that is, there is no place in the heart for the love of God, because it is preoccupied with evil lusts. "Unfruitful": that is, no virtues appear in his life.

13.14.0.en: "Good": that is, the ground that has been plowed and then fertilized and watered, meaning a person's self-examination and repentance, as well as spiritual striving in using the means of grace, of sacraments and spiritual practices.

13.14.1.en: "Heareth the word, and understandeth it": that is, he cares for practical application and not only theoretical knowledge.

13.14.2.en: "Beareth fruit... an hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty": degrees of response and spiritual striving, from which virtues result, and indeed the grace of God increases for those who respond and strive, so this difference among them in holiness appears.

13.15.s.en: (4) The parable of the tares of the field

13.15.0.en: "The kingdom of heaven": that is, the reign of Christ coming from heaven, to reign over the hearts of His children.

13.15.1.en: The man: He is God, who created all human beings in His image and likeness, to live with Him forever in His Kingdom, and to bear good works.

13.16.0.en: "While men slept": the sleep of those responsible for the planting, that is, the priests and servants, and it means the lack of spiritual vigilance and care for the people.

13.16.1.en: The enemy: he is Satan, and he is not an enemy of the husbandmen or the wheat, but of God and all His children. He took advantage of the opportunity of the sleep of the husbandmen responsible for the field, and sowed the seeds of tares, which point to the heresies that the originators of innovations plant in the hearts of some people, and so turn them away from God. Or they signify sins and lusts that defile people, so that they become wicked and do not give the good fruit that God was awaiting from them. "Tares": seeds similar to the seeds of wheat, but they are weeds that harm the original plant, that is, the wheat. "Wheat": grain.

13.16.2.en: "Went his way": in secret, as if he had done nothing, although he is the cause of the evil in the world. My beloved brother... how necessary it is for each of us to be spiritually alert, so as not to accept evil thoughts or lusts that turn us away from God, and if he is a servant, to care for those he serves, lest they turn into tares and be turned away from God.

13.17.0.en: When the seeds grew, the tare plants appeared, that is, foreign weeds, different from the wheat... "by their fruits ye shall know them"; the wheat gave ears, but the tares at the beginning are similar to wheat as a little plant, but when they grew, the known ears of wheat did not appear on them... So the works of the children of God are good, and the works of the wicked are evil.

13.18.0.en: "The servants of the householder": they are the spiritual servants, whether bishops or priests or everyone who serves in the Church, and they noticed that there are wicked people in the world far from God, because their fruits differ from the beloved ears of wheat, and they were greatly astonished at this change, for they had expected good fruits from all the plants, because all God's planting is good.

13.18.1.en: And when they inquired about the reason for the presence of the tares, the householder informed them that an enemy, that is, Satan, had done this, and put seeds in the field, that is, put evil in the hearts of some human beings, so they went away from God and did not give good fruits.

13.18.2.en: So they asked Him: Shall they gather up the tare plants from among the wheat, that is, pass a sentence of destruction on the wicked in the world?

13.19.0.en: God refused to gather up the tares, lest they harm the original wheat plants, in addition to the fact that destroying the wicked deprives them of sufficient opportunity to repent, and may frighten or disturb the children of God, because they see in their God love and tenderness. For if He destroyed all the wicked, they would be terrified and unable to repent and strive because of the intense fear. For Peter who denied repented and became a preacher, and Matthew the tax collector became a disciple, and Paul, who was Saul, the bitter enemy of Christianity, became its servant, and it honored him with the title "the Apostle." Therefore God did not gather up the tares, perhaps by repentance they will turn into wheat.

13.19.1.en: So the wicked are of two kinds: a kind insisting on its wickedness and this will perish, and the other kind will repent and be saved. So we do not gather up the tares lest we root up the wheat with them, that is, the children of God who have fallen into sin and their appearance became like the tares, but they will repent and return to bear good fruit, that is, become good wheat.

13.19.2.en: Seize the opportunity of life to repent and cast off the seeds of the tares, so that you may have good fruit and a pure life with God.

13.20.0.en: God commanded that all the plants be given a full opportunity to grow, so that the righteous may be tested by their rejecting the evils of the wicked around them, and perhaps the wicked may be enlightened by the light of the righteous and repent and return to God. But if the wicked insist on their wickedness, after death they meet a dreadful fate, which is eternal torment into which they are cast in bundles (groups). Just as they were gathered in evil lusts in the world, they continue together in eternal torment. But the righteous are gathered into the barn of God, that is, His Kingdom, so that each one may enjoy fellowship with God, each according to his toil and his fruits.

13.20.1.en: (5) The parables of the mustard seed and the leaven (vv. 31-33):

13.20.2.en: 31- Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, "The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: 32- Which indeed is the least of all seeds: but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof. 33- Another parable spake he unto them; The kingdom of heaven is like unto leaven, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened."

13.21.0.en: The mustard seed: it is the smallest of seeds, but when it is buried in the ground, it is surrounded by darkness and dust, and endures this. And despite its apparent weakness, the Holy Spirit works in it and makes it grow, and it becomes a great tree, larger than the trees of the rest of the herbs, its companions. And because of its size, the birds can find a place in it for their nests.

13.21.1.en: And the mustard seed signifies the Christian or Christ, who endures sufferings and death, and so has a great life in heaven. And by enduring pain and bearing the Cross, a person's thoughts are raised and become heavenly like the birds soaring in the sky.

13.21.2.en: And the mustard seed signifies the good news of the Gospel, and the Church which began as a small group within Judea, and within years spread to the whole world, and embraced many souls who believed and began to praise God like the birds.

13.21.3.en: The mustard seed is like faith, which is tested in afflictions, and so grows and becomes a great tree.

13.22.0.en: The woman: she signifies the Church that hides the leaven, that is, Christ, for by His Incarnation He lives in our midst, and so turns the meal, which is mankind, into spiritually active believers, who influence others and draw them to the faith. "Three measures": they point to the spirit, the soul and the body, that is, Christ when He took our human nature raised us to a spiritual nature by His redemption and the work of His Holy Spirit in us.

13.22.1.en: The woman may also signify the Jews who crucified Christ, and thus by His death and burial He renewed human nature to live with Him.

13.22.2.en: It is also possible that the woman signifies God who put the leaven, or the Church, in the world, that is, the meal, and it drew souls to the faith, and spread in the whole inhabited world quietly and in love.

13.22.3.en: Keep the word of God within you, and apply it in your life so that it works in you and changes your thoughts and your conduct, and continue to meditate on it so that the renewal of your life continues. And then you will influence those around you without feeling it, and draw them to life with God.

13.23.0.en: At this time the teachings of Christ were all in parables. But before this or after it, His teachings were direct, that is, He used all methods of teaching.

13.24.0.en: "The prophet": that is, the seer, and he is Asaph.

13.24.1.en: "Kept secret": the spiritual ordering of God for the salvation of man, which it was difficult for man to understand because of his sins, and which Christ declares in the New Testament, and it is His love for mankind which was in His heart from the foundation of the world and the creation of man.

13.24.2.en: Matthew was accustomed to confirming his words with prophecies, because he addresses the Jews who knew the Holy Scriptures; and God said this in (Ps 78:2): "I will open my mouth in a parable; I will utter dark sayings of old."

13.24.3.en: God's love for you is very great from eternity, and He wants to declare it to you if you open your heart and care to hear Him. And you can do that through your seeking Him by reading the Holy Bible, and being bound to the Church, and hearing spiritual sermons, and your care to learn from everyone, especially the Fathers and spiritual brethren.

13.25.s.en: (7) The interpretation of the parable of the tares of the field

13.25.0.en: The treasure: it signifies Christ who is in the Holy Bible.

13.25.1.en: The field: it signifies the Holy Bible.

13.25.2.en: "For joy thereof": the spiritual consolations that a person receives through spiritual practices, which move him to give up everything in order to continue enjoying this spiritual feeling.

13.25.3.en: And in order for us to acquire the Holy Bible in our hearts, and live by it, and enjoy Christ who is in it, we must remove from our hearts our material attachments, and be ready to give up any of them, and by this we imitate Joseph who left his garment in the hand of his master's wife, and accepted to be cast into prison, and was raised to the throne of Egypt and had riches and authority, and even distributed good things to the whole world around him.

13.25.4.en: And the field also signifies Christ, and the treasure His profound words which the believer submissive to the Holy Spirit understands, who is the one not attached to the world and all its possessions, so that his spirit is free to understand God, and by this God reigns over the heart, and the believer has a portion in the Kingdom of Heaven.

13.26.0.en: The one pearl of great price is the love of Christ, and this merchant is the spiritual man who seeks the truth, and tries to acquire pearls, that is, virtues. But the love of Christ surpasses every virtue, and of course surpasses all the possessions of the world, and likewise all material lusts however dazzling they seem. And in his great amazement at the love of Christ, he gives up all that is in the world and considers it refuse, that he may gain Christ. And then He reigns over his heart as a pledge of the eternal Kingdom.

13.26.1.en: Do not be occupied with the affairs of the world and the needs of the body and the various enticements, rather than the salvation of your soul, but give priority to your relationship with God, and if worldly matters conflict with your spiritual life, be strong and give them up that you may obtain the salvation of your soul, and enjoy serving others to win them by love for Christ.

13.27.0.en: Christ made sure that His disciples understood His parables, so that they would apply them in their lives.

13.28.0.en: Christ made clear to His disciples how to be scribes truly learned in the truth, the word of God, and not like the Jewish scribes who were concerned with copying the Holy Scriptures carefully and with precision in the letter, and not with doing them. So He likened the spiritual scribe, who has learned the word of God, to a man who has a house, which is his life depending on the word of God, and he brings out of the Holy Bible useful meanings, whether from the new (the New Testament) or the old (the Old Testament), to live by them, and they guide him in his life with God.

13.29.0.en: After He had completed His teachings to the crowds and His disciples by these parables, He left the place, and went to another place to continue preaching.

13.29.1.en: Take care to read the Holy Bible in both its Testaments, to obtain spiritual meanings that you apply in your life every day... By this you take care of the salvation of your soul, and then from what you have experienced you will have something to teach others.

13.30.0.en: Jesus came to the city of Nazareth where He was brought up, for He was one of its citizens, and entered their Jewish synagogue and taught His powerful teachings, and they marveled greatly at the power of His words and His miracles. It is good for a person to care for the spiritual care of his family and relatives, and even if this is difficult because of their rejection of his words, he can offer this care by praying for them, and indirect teaching such as speaking about what he heard in the sermons of the Church or reading from the Holy Bible and spiritual books. And if he has a standing with them, let him speak directly, and if not, he can recommend some servants of the Church or loved ones connected with spiritual things to draw them to God.

13.31.0.en: The Jews' wonder did not move them to faith, but they were content only with wonder, since they knew His origin, that He is the son of Mary and Joseph the carpenter, and they also knew the sons and daughters of His mother's sister whose names are mentioned... the sons of Mary, the sister of the Virgin, the wife of Cleophas, and Jewish custom regarded the sons of an aunt and the sons of an uncle as brothers (as is known now in Upper Egypt). So they could not imagine that the awaited Messiah would be an ordinary person coming out from among them, although the prophecies declare this clearly.

13.32.0.en: Because their minds were confined to His human origin and His relatives, they could not believe in His divinity. And there was a common proverb among them that a prophet is without honor in his own country, so because of their knowing His origin they were accustomed to treat Him as an ordinary man and not a distinguished one.

13.32.1.en: And because of the weakness of their faith, He did only few miracles among them, because they would not believe Him.

13.32.2.en: God is ready to work in your life according to your faith and your holding fast to Him and your seeking Him, so open your heart to being discipled and learning at the hands of those around you, and do not belittle any member of your family or your acquaintances, for he may be the divine image that God offers you with simplicity and ease, that you may learn from him, even if he is your little child, or any person of little standing.

13.32.3.en: The killing of John the Baptist; the feeding of the crowds; the walking on water
